incidents.cause: The student pilot's distraction and subsequent loss of airplane control after the cabin window opened during the takeoff roll.
The flight's encounter with the jet wash from a parked commercial airplane while taxiing for takeoff.
Improper maintenance that resulted in contamination of the engine's compressor turbine disc and blade assembly by glass bead remnants, which resulted in a blade failure.
The failure of the ramp agent to use a tail stand.
The pilot's inadequate fuel management, which resulted in fuel starvation and a total loss of engine power during cruise flight.
The pilot’s loss of directional control during the landing.
The flight instructor’s improper landing flare and failure to maintain a proper descent rate during approach, which resulted in a hard landing.

The pilot's failure to maintain directional control of the tailwheel-equipped airplane during landing, which resulted in a ground loop. Contributing to the accident was the flight instructor's failure to adequately monitor the landing.
The student pilot's failure to maintain pitch control during the landing flare, which resulted in a hard landing.
The failure of the student pilot to achieve a proper touchdown during a touch-and-go landing resulting in a hard landing and substantial damage.
